mechanism_claims.entity_scope: dimeric and tetrameric RRWQWR-based peptides against E. faecalis ATCC strains
mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence supports peptide-associated cell-surface morphological alterations in E. faecalis after dimeric or tetrameric treatment; leakage is framed as microscopy-supported morphology, not a quantified membrane-permeabilization assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No live/dead membrane dye, ion leakage, or molecular target assay was found locally; mechanism remains morphology-level evidence.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: dimeric and tetrameric RRWQWR-based peptides against P. aeruginosa ATCC strains
mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence supports peptide-associated P. aeruginosa surface shrinkage, porosity/disrupted membrane morphology, and population changes after treatment, with stronger qualitative damage described for tetrameric treatment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Evidence is qualitative SEM morphology; no exact pore-count or membrane-potential quantification was recoverable from local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion links cationic/hydrophobic peptide features to membrane-surface attraction as a plausible rationale; this is retained as interpretive context rather than direct evidence.
